subject: Re: Discovery recap — Redwood fit for Acme Logistics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Howard <tim.howard@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + recommended next steps

Hi Tim —

Thanks again for taking the time today. A quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a suggested path forward. If anything below is off, tell me and I’ll update.

What we heard:
- Primary objective: reduce per-call inference cost on internal routing engine while keeping 95th pct latency under 180ms.
- Current stack: in-house transformer microservice running on mixed GPU fleet, batch sizes vary widely based on peak windows.
- Data constraints: logs and KV cache can be shared, but PII must not leave the VPC until redaction step.

Initial recommendation (scope):
1) Pilot Redwood Hosted Dedicated for the routing model (2x GPUs, steady-state throughput)
2) Enable prefix KV caching + quantized model variant to hit cost target
3) 4-week technical deep-dive: perf baseline, latency SLO tuning, and security review (SOC 2 evidence)

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf (summary + config proposal), proposed-mop.pdf (mutual action plan draft).

Proposed next steps:
- Are you ok with a 4-week pilot scoped to the routing model?
- If yes, can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (Wed or Thu morning PST)?

I’ll hold Wed/Thu 9–11am PST for now — tell me what works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

---

Subject: Checking fit — quick feedback?

Hi Tim —

I wanted to follow up one last time on the discovery materials I sent and Ben’s note about a week-1 test plan. We’ve seen a handful of similar teams move forward when the pilot lined up with a clear 1) perf baseline and 2) redaction-safe KV cache validation.

If Redwood is not a fit, could you share a quick note with the reason? Options that help us: budget timing, internal infra ownership, security constraints, or roadmap mismatch. Even a one-line reply saves us time and lets me be thoughtful about next steps.

If you are still evaluating and want to keep this open, what would help move it forward — a short (30m) technical call, an internal deck for stakeholders, or an NDA?

If I don’t hear back by end of this week I’ll assume timing is not right and close the loop on our side — we can always reopen later.

Appreciate the candid feedback either way.

Thanks,
Marissa
